external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A sensor node installed on a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We have a few thousand sensor nodes installed on customer sites.
external_entities.notes: The nodes are outside the organisation's physical control.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An internal operator who views telemetry dashboards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that receives sensor readings and forwards accepted readings.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that consumes readings and writes them to the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used to check the device key and determine which customer a node belongs to.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A Pub/Sub service carrying accepted sensor readings to the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery telemetry store containing site addresses and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: firmware bucket
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket from which sensor nodes poll firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.description: A sensor node publishes readings to the device gateway.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.description: The device gateway looks up the device registry to check the key and identify the customer.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.description: The device gateway forwards accepted readings onto Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer picks up readings from Pub/Sub.
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.description: The telemetry normalizer writes readings into the telemetry lake.
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery

data_flows.name: poll image
data_flows.description: A sensor node polls the firmware bucket for a new firmware image.
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_flows.notes: The bucket is public read, so node authentication to the bucket is not stated as required.

data_flows.name: service console
data_flows.description: A field technician services a sensor node over its local serial console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: Authentication is unknown: "I don't know what authentication that console has, if any."

data_flows.name: view dashboards
data_flows.description: A fleet operator views dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

trust_boundaries.name: customer site
trust_boundaries.description: A customer-controlled site where sensor nodes are installed.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.name: GKE
trust_boundaries.description: The GKE environment where the device gateway runs.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE

trust_boundaries.name: analytics network
trust_boundaries.description: The network containing the telemetry normalizer.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network from which fleet operators access dashboards.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry contains credentials because the gateway uses it to check the device key.
assumptions.basis: The gateway looks up the device registry "to check the key".

assumptions.assumption: The device registry contains customer-identifying information because it records which customer a node belongs to.
assumptions.basis: The gateway uses the registry "to find out which customer the node belongs to".

assumptions.assumption: The device registry is confidential because it contains a device key and customer association.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the registry is used to check the key and identify the customer.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake is confidential because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns described as customer data.
assumptions.basis: The source states: "The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data."

assumptions.assumption: The device gateway presents a non-web interface because it is an MQTT broker.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies the gateway as "an MQTT broker".

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry normalizer presents a non-web interface because it is a Python consumer rather than a web application.
assumptions.basis: The source identifies it as "a Python consumer" in the analytics network.
